## Body

#306 (F249) and #308 (F256). The canary takes the runtime model from the seat's native transcript (unisphere model.current, basis native) and uses the pane footer as a fallback. Both are same-user self-reports. Under C33 the canary catches accidental misattribution only; it is not proof against a seat lying on purpose. Say that explicitly in any verdict.

Traps to check:
- Option/unknown mapping. Unisphere's pending_switch is None when it can't order the switch against the last call (pending_known=false). Count "model.pending_switch" in status.unknown as pending, never as none (S306-N1).
- The record misses switches. Unisphere counts only default-role model_change, while OMP also switches for its smol, slow, temporary, fallback and prewalk roles. The OMP footer agreement check (omp_model_shows against the native selector's own catalog row) is the only guard against those switches.
- `if let Ok(false)` is a fail-open. A helper Err (omp models down, its 5 s timeout, no catalog row) must refuse, not skip the check (S306-003, fixed in #308 as RuntimeModel::Unchecked). Grep for that pattern in any guard.
- observe_bind copies the native_session_id argument straight into its facts. Comparing the two is tautological, so removing that comparison loses nothing. Check that a freshness guard reads something it observed, not its own argument.
- Refusals return before service.mutation.lock() and go only to the caller's HTTP envelope. catalog_error carries omp's trimmed stderr, which is not size-capped. That exposure already existed on the resolve path.

Open: N306-R2-01, a provider switch that keeps the same display name, sits upstream as F257.
